title: Compute-Optimal Scaling Laws for Spiking Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.15146v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Spiking neural networks target energy-efficient language modeling through sparse, binary activations, but the efficiency-accuracy tradeoff of spiking language models is uncharacterized at scale. We present the first Chinchilla-style IsoFLOP scaling study of a spiking language model, sweeping SpikeGPT-family models (RWKV backbone) from width 384 to 1536 across compute budgets from $3\times10^{17}$ to $10^{19}$ FLOPs on FineWeb-EDU. We report two findings. First, the compute-optimal frontier is $N_{opt} \propto C^{0.56}$, close to the 0.50 that Hoffmann et al. report for dense Transformers, so spiking does not change how parameters and data should be traded off under a compute budget. Second, against non-spiking RWKV and Transformer baselines trained the same way, the loss gap splits into a backbone cost of about 0.16 nats that does not change with compute and a spiking cost that falls steadily with compute, from 0.34 to 0.23 nat

translated_title: 脉冲语言模型的计算最优缩放定律
translated_abstract: 脉冲神经网络通过稀疏的二值激活实现节能的语言建模，但脉冲语言模型在大规模下的效率-精度权衡尚未被刻画。我们首次对脉冲语言模型进行了Chinchilla式的IsoFLOP缩放研究，在FineWeb-EDU数据集上，于3×10¹⁷至10¹⁹ FLOPs的计算预算范围内，对SpikeGPT系列模型（采用RWKV骨干，宽度从384到1536）进行了系统扫描。我们报告了两个发现：首先，计算最优前沿为 N_opt ∝ C^0.56，接近Hoffmann等人报告的密集Transformer的0.50，因此脉冲化并不改变在给定计算预算下参数与数据应如何权衡；其次，与以相同方式训练的非脉冲RWKV和Transformer基线相比，损失差距可分解为不随计算量变化的约0.16 nats的骨干成本，以及随计算量稳步下降的脉冲成本（从0.34降至0.23 nats）。
tldr: 本文首次对脉冲语言模型开展Chinchilla式缩放研究，发现其计算最优缩放指数（0.56）与密集Transformer（0.50）接近，且脉冲化带来的损失代价随计算预算增加而稳步下降。
en_tdlr: This paper presents the first Chinchilla-style scaling study of spiking language models, showing their compute-optimal scaling exponent (0.56) closely matches dense Transformers (0.50) and that the spiking loss penalty steadily decreases with increasing compute.
